title: Dominic (1170–1221)
hookLine: a Spanish canon starts an order of preachers who live poor and study hard

lines: THE SAME MAN BUILDS ON STUDY.
cards: A student in a Spanish town is selling his books. In his day a book was handwritten on parchment, slow and costly, and these carry his own notes in the margins.
But there's a famine, and people in the streets are starving. Jordan of Saxony, who knew him and wrote an early account of him, says he sold the books and gave the money away.
A brother remembered him saying he would not study on dead skins while living people died of hunger. Years later, the same man would found an order built around study. His name was Dominic.

teach.b: Dominic became a canon, a priest living in community at the cathedral of Osma, and traveled north with his bishop, Diego.
In the south of France they found preachers arriving with horses and servants and fine clothes, and being ignored. People there were listening to wandering teachers who lived poor.
Diego and Dominic, Jordan says, drew a plain conclusion: if you want to be heard, go on foot, with nothing, the way the apostles went.
Dominic gathered a small band of preachers, and the Church approved them as a new kind of religious order: not monks staying in one monastery, but friars sent out.
They begged for their food, owned little, and went where people were.
Jesus's charge at the end of Mark, in the Douay-Rheims, was their whole job description: "Go ye into the whole world, and preach the gospel to every creature." Then the books came back.

teach.h: SENT TO STUDY, AND STUDY HARD.
teach.b: A preacher needs something true to say, so Dominic sent his brothers to study, and study hard, in towns where the schools were.
The student who sold his books for the hungry now asked his brothers to fill their heads, so they could feed people another way.
Thomas Aquinas, a Dominican himself, later wrote that it is a greater thing to contemplate and pass on to others what you've contemplated than only to contemplate.

teach.h: PREACH THE GOSPEL TO EVERY CREATURE.
teach.b: Dominicans took that as their own, and still sign their names with the letters O.P., for the Order of Preachers. Prayer, then study, then the handing on.

how: Dominican friars and sisters, and lay Dominicans, live a rhythm of prayer, study and preaching, and Dominican friars write O.P. after their names for the Order of Preachers.

o: the bishop who sent friars to the sultan
the monk who founded the abbey of Cluny
the friar who founded the Order of Preachers

s: Dominic's friars stayed in one monastery like monks
they were friars, sent out on foot to preach where people were.
Dominic once sold his own books during a famine
Jordan of Saxony says he sold them; a brother remembered him refusing to study on dead skins while people starved.
Dominic told his brothers to stop studying
he sent them to study hard, so they could preach well.

games.q: you're a student in a famine. your handwritten books are your most precious things. people are starving in the street. what do you do?
o: keep studying; you'll help more people later.
sell the books and give the money to the hungry.
ask your teachers to organize a collection.
games.why: Dominic sold them. he would not study on dead skins, a brother remembered him saying, while living people died of hunger. later he made study central to his order.

practice: Choose one thing you've heard many times and never really thought about: a line from the Creed, a verse, a word from this path.
Turn it over slowly, asking what each word says and what you'd ask someone wise sitting next to you, without reaching for a conclusion. If you pray, let the study become prayer.

wordCard.voice: Dominic. He sold his books to feed the hungry, then founded the friars who study hard and preach, known as the Order of Preachers. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: the Order of Preachers, the source of the letters O.P.

carryVoice: Your line: to contemplate and to share. What you take in is meant to be handed on. Until tomorrow.
